messages:
incident-bot: P0 — High error rate delivering Stripe webhooks detected. 1,180 failed deliveries in last 6m, error ratio 20% (threshold 5%). Rule: webhooks.delivery.errors > 5% for 5m. Alert page: https://redwood.inc/alerts/WEBHOOKS-STRIPE-493

ashley (on-call): paging @maria @jordan. I'm on call, looking at the webhook-forwarder logs. Seeing a ton of 429/401s and some 500s to stripe.com.

maria (SRE): on it, pulling recent responses. Can you dump a few samples?

ashley (on-call): sure, snippet from the forwarder:
```
2025-10-02T14:11:03Z | POST https://hooks.stripe.com/v1/events -> 429 Too Many Requests 
headers: Retry-After: 30, x-stripe-requests-remaining: 0 
body: {"error":{"type":"rate_limit_error","message":"Too many requests to Stripe API"}}
```

jordan (eng): also seeing intermittent 401s for a subset of webhook requests:
```
2025-10-02T14:12:45Z | POST https://hooks.stripe.com/v1/events -> 401 Unauthorized 
body: {"error":{"message":"Invalid API key provided"}}
```

maria (SRE): hmm. Two distinct classes: rate limits (429) from Stripe and auth failures (401) for some keys. Could be a rotated key or a bad secret in the queue.

ashley (on-call): impact: customers using webhook-driven flows (webhook -> sync -> UI update) may see billing and subscription status delayed. Support tickets might show "payment pending" states.

kevin (support): already getting messages from a few enterprise customers reporting invoices still in "pending" after paying. CS escalation queued. Can we surface a short customer-facing blurb for the status page?

lisa (sales): flagging top-10 accounts: Acme, BrightLayer, HealthQ — they rely on immediate webhook processing for subscription gating. They should be notified ASAP.

maria (SRE): immediate mitigations: 1) identify and rotate any bad webhook secret in our queue; 2) pause non-critical webhook types (subscription.schedule and invoice.upcoming) to reduce pressure; 3) enable fallback polling for critical billing events via Stripe Events API.

jordan (eng): I can push a hotfix to the webhook-forwarder to skip replays for events with invalid auth and surface them to a dead-letter queue for manual inspection. Also will add a circuit-breaker to reduce retries to Stripe when 429 spikes.

ashley (on-call): implementing steps now. Maria, can you open a ticket with Stripe and request quota lift / explain unusual auth failures?

maria (SRE): opened ticket with Stripe support. Ticket #SR-842739. Status: awaiting initial triage. Linked to our account and provided logs + sample request ids. stripe-support-bot: Stripe: Received SR-842739, initial triage started. ETA: 30–60m.

ashley (on-call): rolling config change to pause non-critical types: `WEBHOOK_FORWARD_WHITELIST=charge.succeeded,invoice.payment_succeeded,customer.subscription.updated` — removing lower-priority webhooks for now. Pushing via deploy bot.
deploy-bot: deploy started by ashley (webhook-forwarder:hotfix/skip-invalid-keys)

deploy-bot: deploy successful in us-east-1 (canary 1/2 passed)

jordan (eng): canary looks good. Forwarder now sends only whitelisted events and stops retry storms for invalid auth. Also created a temporary polling worker: `stripe-poller-temp` that will call `/v1/events` with `type[]=charge.succeeded&type[]=invoice.payment_succeeded` and process in idempotent mode.

ashley (on-call): started the poller. Initial catch: 2,200 events in backlog; throttling ingestion to 200/s to avoid downstream pressure.

kevin (support): drafting status page message: "Investigating — some customers experiencing delayed billing updates due to Stripe webhook delivery issues. We're processing backlog and using a temporary polling fallback. No data loss expected. Updates every 30m." Approve?

lisa (sales): yes, please include line for enterprise accounts we contacted directly.

maria (SRE): monitoring metrics: webhook error rate dropped from 20% -> 4.5% after whitelist + circuit-breaker. Poller catch-up progressing ~180 events/min.

jordan (eng): note: we found ~0.3% of events in the backlog have malformed signatures (old signing secret), they were moved to DLQ. Will coordinate key rotation via ops-admin.

maria (SRE): contacting infra to rotate keys for the affected webhook routing entries.

ashley (on-call): handoff: I need to step out for 30m. @maria take lead for next 2 hrs. @jordan you own the poller and DLQ processing. I'll be available on pager if anything spikes.

maria (SRE): taking lead. Next check-in at +30m. Current severity: P1 -> keeping P0 until catch-up < 1% and Stripe confirms quota/auth root cause.

stripe-support-bot: SR-842739 update: Rate-limiting observed on our ingestion layer in region us-east-1, engineering investigating. We will provide a timeline in next 45m.

kevin (support): CS playbook: suggest telling customers to expect up to 2h delay for billing UI, provide workaround: manual refresh or check receipts. For any customer blocking revenue flow, escalate to SRE on-call immediately.

lisa (sales): I emailed top-10 with note we have a mitigation and are doing a controlled replay; offering a dedicated Slack channel for them.

maria (SRE): long-term actions added to incident board: 1) improve webhook secret rotation detection; 2) exponential backoff + global token bucket for forwarder; 3) implement event-stream fallback in product; 4) run Chaos test for Stripe rate-limit scenarios. Assigning to jordan for implementation.

jordan (eng): acknowledged. Will open RFC and schedule work.

ashley (on-call): status update for ops: backlog decreasing, forwarder stable, Stripe triage pending. Leaving incident in progress. Postmortem owner: jordan (eng).
